title: Complete algebra devissages survive arbitrary pointed base change
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to R\prime$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $A$ generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra. Let $N$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $\mathfrak p\prime\subset R\prime$ be prime ideals with inverse image $\mathfrak p$, and suppose $N/A/R$ has a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p$ [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage]. Put $A\prime=A\otimes_R R\prime$ and $N\prime=N\otimes_R R\prime$, with their natural $R\prime$-algebra and $A\prime$-module structures [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $A\prime$ is of finite type over $R\prime$, $N\prime$ is a finite $A\prime$-module, and $N\prime/A\prime/R\prime$ has a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p\prime$. More precisely, for every given devissage $(A_i,B_i,M_i,\alpha_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$, tensoring every algebra, module and map with $R\prime$ over $R$ gives such a devissage of the same length. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $R\to R\prime$ is imposed; a devissage of length zero is included.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), its proof applied to the algebra data of Tag 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra); affine comparison Tag 05I0 (remark-same-notion). The algebra version omits the extra relative-dimension condition, which is not used in the base-change proof.

proof.text: Fix the given complete devissage and write $A_i'=A_i\otimes_RR'$, $B_i'=B_i\otimes_RR'$, $M_i'=M_i\otimes_RR'$ and $\alpha_i'=\alpha_i\otimes_R1$. The free source identifies with $(B_i')^{\oplus r_i}$: send $e_jb\otimes t$ to $e_j(b\otimes t)$, with inverse sending $e_j(b\otimes t)$ to $e_jb\otimes t$. All these maps and scalar actions are defined by the tensor relations. For an $R$-algebra $E$, if $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ generate an $E$-module $M$, then $m_j\otimes1$ generate $M\otimes_RR'$ over $E\otimes_RR'$, since $(\sum e_jm_j)\otimes t=\sum(e_j\otimes t)(m_j\otimes1)$. Apply this to $N$ over $A$, each $M_i$ over $A_i$, and each $A_i$ over $B_i$. The images $a_j\otimes1$ of any finite algebra-generating family $a_j$ for $A/R$ generate $A'/R'$: expand each pure tensor using its polynomial expression in the $a_j$. This proves all the module-finiteness assertions and finite type of $A'$.

source.place: Tag 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), conditions (3) and (5); Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), algebra form; Algebra Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), elementary generator argument for (1) and (3)

proof.text: For each original surjection $C\to D$ (namely $A\to A_1$ and $B_i\to A_{i+1}$), tensor its right exact sequence $C\to D\to0$ over $R$ with $R'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] the map $C'=C\otimes_RR'\to D'=D\otimes_RR'$ is surjective. It is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], applied to $C\to D$ and $C\to C'$. Here the required identification $D\otimes_CC'\cong D'$ sends $d\otimes(c\otimes t)$ to $dc\otimes t$, with inverse $d\otimes t\mapsto d\otimes(1\otimes t)$; the balancing relations show these are mutually inverse algebra maps. Thus the first and third kinds of algebra map retain both required properties. The finite maps $B_i'\to A_i'$ were handled by the explicit module generators in step 1.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), via Tag 05H7 (lemma-base-change-one-step), preservation of closed immersions of finite presentation; Tag 05HX conditions (1)-(3)

proof.text: By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], smoothness of $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ agrees with smoothness of the affine ring map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] to see that $R'\to B_i'$ is smooth, and likewise after any further ring base change. Its fibres are geometrically irreducible: for a prime $\mathfrak t'\subset R'$ with inverse image $\mathfrak t\subset R$, and any field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak t')$, the fibre after extension to $L$ has ring $B_i\otimes_R L=(B_i\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak t))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak t)}L$. It is irreducible by the original geometric irreducibility and [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The tensor identifications here are given on pure tensors by multiplication in $L$, with inverse inserting $1$, as in step 2. This proves the smooth geometrically irreducible fibre condition for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 05H7 (lemma-base-change-one-step), smoothness and geometrically irreducible fibres; More on Morphisms Tag 0555 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-irreducible); Tag 05HX condition (4)

proof.text: Put $D=R'/\mathfrak p'$ and $C=B_i'/\mathfrak p'B_i'$. By right exactness, $C=B_i'\otimes_{R'}D$, with the map sending $b\otimes\bar t$ to $\overline{tb}$. Thus $C$ is smooth over the domain $D$ by step 3, and flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Tensoring the injection $D\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ with $C$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Its target is the generic fibre $C\otimes_D\operatorname{Frac}(D)=B_i'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, using the residue-field fraction description of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This fibre is irreducible by step 3 and reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]; hence it is a nonzero domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The unital subring $C$ is therefore a nonzero domain as well, so $\mathfrak q_i'=\mathfrak p'B_i'$ is prime. This is only the elementary subring-of-a-domain argument after the cited exactness theorem; it does not require $R'$, or $R\to R'$, to be flat.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), generic-fibre condition; Tag 05HX condition (7); compare Tag 05FS (lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective), proof: extended primes for geometrically integral flat fibres

proof.text: The inverse image of $\mathfrak q_i'$ in $B_i$ is exactly $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak pB_i$. Indeed $R/\mathfrak p\hookrightarrow R'/\mathfrak p'$ is injective by the pointed hypothesis, while $B_i/\mathfrak pB_i$ is smooth, hence flat over $R/\mathfrak p$, by smooth base change and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to this injection to obtain an injection $B_i/\mathfrak pB_i\hookrightarrow(B_i/\mathfrak pB_i)\otimes_{R/\mathfrak p}(R'/\mathfrak p')=B_i'/\mathfrak p'B_i'$. The last identification is the quotient tensor map from step 4 and balancing from step 2. Consequently precisely the elements of $\mathfrak q_i$ vanish in that quotient. Localizing the induced injection of domains and taking fractions gives the field map $\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_i')$, explicitly $\bar b/\bar c\mapsto\overline{b\otimes1}/\overline{c\otimes1}$ for $c\notin\mathfrak q_i$; denominators stay nonzero by the injection.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), residue-field extension at the generic fibre points; Tag 05HX condition (7)

proof.text: For $L_i=\kappa(\mathfrak q_i')$ there is an isomorphism $M_i'\otimes_{B_i'}L_i\cong(M_i\otimes_{B_i}\kappa(\mathfrak q_i))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q_i)}L_i$. Both sides identify with $M_i\otimes_{B_i}L_i$. On the left use $(m\otimes t)\otimes l\mapsto m\otimes tl$ with inverse $m\otimes l\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes l$; on the right use $(m\otimes u)\otimes l\mapsto m\otimes ul$ with inverse $m\otimes l\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes l$. The tensor relations prove these identities. The analogous free-source maps send each $e_j$ to $e_j$. On $e_j\otimes l$, the new generic-fibre map is therefore the old generic-fibre map tensored with $L_i$. Tensor the inverse of the old isomorphism as well: preservation of composition and identity gives a two-sided inverse. Thus $\alpha_i'\otimes_{B_i'}L_i$ is an isomorphism, with no exactness or flatness assumption on $R'$ used here.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), displayed residue-field tensor isomorphism in its proof; Tag 05HX condition (7)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] over $R$ to $(B_i)^{\oplus r_i}\xrightarrow{\alpha_i}M_i\to\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i)\to0$. Using the free-source identification in step 1 gives $\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i')\cong\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i)\otimes_RR'$: the induced quotient map is surjective and its kernel is exactly the image of $\alpha_i'$. It is $B_i'$-linear, since the tensor of the original $B_i$-linear quotient map respects the action $(b\otimes t)(m\otimes u)=bm\otimes tu$. Tensor the given isomorphisms $N\cong M_1$ and $\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i)\cong M_{i+1}$ and their inverses. Functoriality gives $N'\cong M_1'$ over $A'$ and $\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i')\cong M_{i+1}'$ over $B_i'$. Finally $\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_n')\cong0\otimes_RR'=0$. Thus no assertion about preservation of kernels, and no flatness of $R'$, enters the cokernel argument.

source.place: Tag 05HJ (lemma-base-change-complete), cokernel commutation with base change; Tag 05HX conditions (5), (6), (8)

proof.text: Steps 1-7 verify every datum and condition of [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage], retaining the same index set, ranks and maps tensored with $R'$. Hence they give the required complete devissage of length $n$. If $n=0$, the definition says $N=0$, so $N'=0$ by the tensor relations and the empty sequence is the required length-zero devissage. The finite-type and finite-module conclusions were proved independently in step 1, including this case.
